portfolio_context: Actual holding, tax basis and portfolio risk budget were not supplied. No position size is invented and no trade authorization is implied.
structural_thesis: SANIL is scaling from a niche custom distribution/special-transformer manufacturer into a larger US-grid, data-center/renewable and eventually ultra-high-voltage power-equipment supplier. The business has genuine customer-qualification and execution advantages, but the current investment case depends on sustaining unusually high margins while diversifying a very concentrated customer/geography mix and deploying new capacity at high returns.
current_finding: H1 2026 revenue rose 38.5% YoY to KRW314.5B, operating profit rose 40.4% to KRW117.5B and OPM reached 37.4%. Backlog was KRW556.8B versus KRW448.8B at FY2025, utilization was 87.2%, and a KRW51.2B TMEIC USA reactor contract was disclosed after the half-year. Growth quality is strong, but H1 top-four customers represented about 89.5% of sales and the US represented about 87%.
economic_finding: TTM revenue is about KRW589.4B, operating profit KRW212.4B, net income KRW180.3B and OCF KRW187.6B. Mechanical OCF less tangible and intangible capex is about KRW171.0B. Normalized owner cash is underwritten at KRW170-195B, central KRW180B. At KRW198,000, central owner cash trades at about 33.7x, ~3.0% owner-cash yield.
capital_and_survival: Balance-sheet risk is low: H1 equity was KRW663.3B, liabilities KRW94.4B, bank borrowings were effectively zero and the company held a large cash/financial-asset pool. The KRW69.25B property acquisition for ultra-high-voltage capacity is self-funded and financially manageable, though it raises execution and return-on-capital risk.
permanent_loss_case: Transformer scarcity and US renewable/data-center investment normalize while industry capacity catches up; SANIL remains concentrated in a few customers, loses pricing power, raw-material inflation compresses margins and the ultra-high-voltage expansion earns below expectations. Owner cash stagnates or declines, operating margin falls toward the low-20s, and the market rerates the stock from a premium structural-growth multiple to an ordinary cyclical industrial multiple.

evidence: Revenue expanded from KRW214.5B in 2023 to KRW501.9B in 2025; H1 2026 grew another 38.5% YoY.
Second-factory ramp, KRW42B 2026 equipment/automation program and August property acquisition create a clear capacity path.
Founder/co-CEO retains a large stake and execution in US markets is proven.
counter_evidence: Founder spouse sold a large block and the co-CEO monetized most of a recent option exercise.
Ultra-high-voltage entry is outside the historical <=72.5kV core.

evidence: Custom transformers/reactors are safety-critical and engineered to customer specifications.
Sales are largely direct to top-tier inverter makers, US utilities and end customers.
Backlog reached KRW556.8B and a further KRW51.2B TMEIC contract was disclosed after H1.
counter_evidence: Customer identities and contract economics are confidential.

evidence: Qualification, reliability history, custom engineering and after-service create entry friction.
DOE evidence confirms persistent transformer shortages and long lead times.
counter_evidence: The moat is operational rather than patent-protected and peers can add capacity.
Shortage conditions may temporarily flatter competitive strength.

evidence: TTM OCF is ~KRW187.6B and mechanical OCF-capex ~KRW171.0B.
H1 OCF rose to KRW90.1B from KRW17.9B while bank debt remained near zero.
Recent capacity additions coincided with rapid sales/profit growth and >35% operating margins.
counter_evidence: Margins may partly reflect scarcity pricing/product mix.

evidence: Core factory investment is self-funded and aligned with demand.
Balance sheet remains conservative and audit/ICFR evidence is clean.
counter_evidence: KRW29.5B private-equity partnership commitment is non-core.
Large spouse block sale and co-CEO option monetization weaken alignment.
Small Alborz Cable related-party payable remains unresolved because of US Iran sanctions.

evidence: H1 liabilities/equity was ~14% and bank borrowings effectively zero.
Cash/financial assets materially exceed disclosed near-term property/capex payments.
Credit rating improved to A+ in April 2026.
counter_evidence: Not all financial assets are instantly distributable cash.

evidence: At KRW198,000 the stock is ~33.7x central owner cash, ~3.0% yield.
At 10% discount the full reverse DCF requires ~11.5% 10-year owner-cash/share CAGR at 20x terminal and ~10.7% at 22x.
Expectations have compressed from the 52-week high.
counter_evidence: The valuation still assumes durable double-digit compounding from a ~36% TTM operating-margin base.
Base-case DCF is below the reference price.

evidence: US grid replacement, AI/data-center load, renewables/ESS and supply bottlenecks provide multiple structural drivers.
US share remains small and successful ultra-high-voltage entry can expand ASP/TAM.
counter_evidence: Operating leverage can reverse when capacity catches up.

evidence: FY2025/H1 2026 auditor disclosures are clean and FY2025 ICFR audit was unqualified.
items.resolution_needed: Escalate if related-party items grow or disclosure/control failures emerge.

evidence: Core operations generate strong cash, bank borrowings are near zero and property acquisition is internally funded.
items.resolution_needed: Reassess if expansion requires material debt/equity issuance.

evidence: H1 share count rose ~0.56% from option exercises; dilution is not yet persistent/material relative to owner-cash growth.
items.resolution_needed: Monitor remaining options and annual diluted-share growth.

evidence: Revenue growth is accompanied by backlog growth, rising OCF, high margins and falling receivables.
items.resolution_needed: Escalate if backlog/order growth decouples from cash conversion.

evidence: Recent factory investment coincided with strong sales, profit and owner-cash growth without leverage.
Backlog and post-period TMEIC order show no current customer-trust/qualification erosion.
items.resolution_needed: Escalate if win rates/backlog/margins weaken faster than industry demand.

evidence: At 10% discount the market requires ~10.7%-12.4% 10-year owner-cash/share CAGR for 22x-18x terminal multiples—demanding but not objectively bull-only given current growth/capacity expansion.
items.resolution_needed: Reassess if normalized owner cash is below KRW170B or long-run margins fall materially.

evidence: H1 top four customers were ~89.5% of revenue; US ~87% and renewable/special-transformer mix ~76%. FY2025 top-five share was ~61%.
items.resolution_needed: Need rolling evidence no single customer remains above ~25%, top-four trends toward <70%, and grid/data-center/utility/ultra-high-voltage demand broadens without margin/cash deterioration.

evidence: Low leverage, high cash generation and tangible grid demand reduce financing-failure risk; main permanent-loss path is valuation/margin compression.
items.resolution_needed: Escalate if owner cash declines while expansion capital rises and concentration stays extreme.

valuation.reverse_expectations: At 10% discount, required constant 10-year owner-cash/share CAGR is ~12.4% at 18x terminal, ~11.5% at 20x, ~10.7% at 22x and ~9.5% at 25x.

attacks: Transformer shortage may be temporary; industry capacity can normalize price/margin.
Top-four customers are ~89.5%; one program delay can materially hit results.
US is ~87% of H1 revenue, concentrating policy/FX/capex-cycle risk.
Renewable/special transformers are ~76% of H1 mix, exposing project timing/policy risk.
Backlog is ~0.95x TTM revenue and typical delivery 3-6 months, not multi-year recurring revenue.
~36% TTM operating margin may be above normalized scarcity/mix economics.
Copper/aluminum inflation may outrun pass-through despite procurement mitigation.
Ultra-high-voltage entry has new qualification/testing/competitive risks.
Non-core investments, option monetization and related-party cleanup weaken the simple owner-operator story.
At ~33.7x owner cash, single-digit growth plus multiple normalization can produce poor returns.
red_team.strongest_bear_thesis: SANIL is a high-quality beneficiary of a temporary transformer supercycle rather than a durable compounder. Supply scarcity and renewable/data-center buildout lift margins; customers remain concentrated, peers add capacity and new ultra-high-voltage investment earns lower returns. Owner cash flattens and the stock rerates to an ordinary industrial multiple.
hidden_assumptions: 36-37% operating margin has a durable structural component.
Customer concentration is timing/program mix rather than fragile dependence.
New capacity fills without price concessions or working-capital deterioration.
The <=72.5kV moat transfers to ultra-high-voltage products.
red_team.independence: Same analyst/model performed the red-team; not an independent second-party review.

falsifiers: Quarterly new orders fall below revenue for two consecutive quarters and backlog falls below ~0.7x TTM revenue.
A top customer is lost/delayed or top-four concentration stays above ~85% for four quarters while orders slow.
Operating margin falls below 28% for two consecutive quarters without a credible temporary investment explanation.
TTM OCF/net income falls below 0.7 or receivables/inventory grow much faster than sales for two quarters.
Owner cash/share fails to grow ~20% cumulatively over two years despite expansion.
Ultra-high-voltage facility/qualification is materially delayed or requires debt-funded capex well beyond disclosed plans.
Material warranty/quality failure damages repeat orders or customer qualification.
increase_evidence: Rolling new orders/backlog remain above ~1.0-1.1x TTM revenue while customer concentration declines.
US revenue broadens into utilities/data-center/EPC/grid customers without margin deterioration.
2027 capacity ramp drives >15% owner-cash/share growth with operating margin >~32% and diluted shares broadly flat.
Ultra-high-voltage line obtains verified qualifications/commercial orders before or alongside major equipment spend.
Cash conversion stays near or above earnings after capex/inventory normalization.
A valuation reset toward ~25x or lower normalized owner cash improves the expectation gap; price alone does not resolve concentration.
sell_evidence: Backlog declines >25% YoY or a major customer cancels/re-sources and replacement orders do not appear.
Operating margin structurally falls into the low-20s while capacity expands.
Expansion/non-core investments require material net debt while owner cash deteriorates.
Persistent option dilution outpaces per-share owner-cash growth.
Repeated large non-core investments displace demonstrably high-return core reinvestment.
Accounting/internal-control weakness or material related-party/regulatory issue compromises integrity.

source_quality.primary: User-supplied DART annual, half-year and asset-acquisition filings dominate financial/customer/backlog/capacity/governance facts; issuer IR/disclosure pages supplement events.
source_quality.secondary: Reuters/US DOE for industry context; Korean disclosure-republication press for post-H1 TMEIC contract; Investing.com only for Sep-14 price.
source_quality.limitations: Customer identities/pricing are confidential; post-H1 official backlog unavailable; broker target prices/capacity estimates excluded from valuation authority; current share count includes a minor post-H1 option-exercise adjustment.
